mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the inertia of a body at rest?

options.A: A body at rest will remain at rest only if a continuous force is applied.
options.B: A body at rest will remain at rest unless acted upon by an external force.
options.C: A body at rest will start moving on its own after some time.
options.D: A body at rest will move only if the surface beneath it is rough.

mcqs.answer: A body at rest will remain at rest unless acted upon by an external force.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of rest means an object that is stationary stays stationary unless a net external force acts on it. Option B states this correctly. Option A is wrong because no continuous force is needed to keep it at rest. Option C suggests spontaneous motion, which contradicts inertia. Option D links motion to surface roughness, which is irrelevant to the concept of inertia of rest.

mcqs.question: A hockey puck slides on a smooth ice surface and continues to move. Which reasoning best explains this observation based on the concept of inertia of motion?

options.A: The ice continuously pushes the puck forward.
options.B: There is no net external force acting on the puck, so its state of motion is maintained.
options.C: The puck’s mass increases as it slides, keeping it moving.
options.D: Gravity pulls the puck forward along the ice.

mcqs.answer: There is no net external force acting on the puck, so its state of motion is maintained.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion states that an object in motion will keep moving with the same speed and direction unless acted upon by a net external force. On smooth ice, friction (the external force) is minimal, so the puck maintains its motion, making option B correct. Option A incorrectly attributes a continuous forward push. Option C is false; mass does not increase during motion. Option D confuses the direction of gravitational force, which acts vertically, not horizontally.

mcqs.question: Which of the following situations best illustrates the inertia of direction?

options.A: A book lying on a table remains stationary until pushed.
options.B: A car moving straight continues straight unless the driver steers or another force acts.
options.C: A ball dropped from a height falls vertically due to gravity.
options.D: A satellite stays in orbit because Earth’s gravity continuously pulls it toward the centre.

mcqs.answer: A car moving straight continues straight unless the driver steers or another force acts.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of direction refers to the tendency of a moving object to continue in the same straight line unless acted upon by an external force. The car moving straight exemplifies this, so option B is correct. Option A shows inertia of rest, not direction. Option C describes free fall, which involves a change in direction due to gravity, not the object's resistance to changing direction. Option D involves centripetal force maintaining orbital motion, not the object's inherent resistance to changing direction.

mcqs.question: In which of the following everyday phenomena does the concept of inertia play the most direct role?

options.A: A passenger feels thrown forward when a bus suddenly stops.
options.B: Water boils faster in a metal pot than in a plastic pot.

mcqs.answer: A passenger feels thrown forward when a bus suddenly stops.
mcqs.explanation: When the bus stops abruptly, the passenger’s body tends to continue moving forward due to its inertia (the resistance of the body’s state of motion to change). This is a direct illustration of inertia. Option B involves thermal conductivity, not inertia. Option C concerns magnetic attraction. Option D is about phototropism, a biological response, not inertia.
